evidence.title: SB 197 House Committee Substitute 1 (2026-03-27)
evidence.supports: Shows HB 593-style data center electric-service tariff, $75,000 minimum application fee, and 25 MW dedicated-resource provisions were inserted into SB 197 as a vehicle around the time HB 593 stalled in the Senate.
evidence.quote: A municipal electric utility shall issue and maintain a tariff... Payment of an initial nonrefundable application fee with a minimum fee of not less than seventy-five thousand dollars ($75,000)...

evidence.title: SB 197 final enacted text
evidence.supports: Confirms the data center provisions carried in SB 197 HCS1 do not appear in the final enacted text, i.e. the HB 593 policy language ultimately died for 2026.
evidence.quote: No occurrences of 'data center' found in the final enacted bill text.

decisions.notes: HB 593 itself never passed the Senate and is dead as a standalone bill (failed_died). Its substantive data center provisions were subsequently inserted into SB 197 (the state government budget vehicle) via House Committee Substitute 1 on 2026-03-27, but were removed in House Committee Substitute 2 (2026-04-15), the version that actually passed both chambers. SB 197 itself was enacted (see KY:SB 197 (2026 RS)), but without any data center policy language, so the HB 593 policy did not become law in 2026.

fields.status: Enacted as Acts Ch. 202 with Governor line-item vetoes 2026-04-27; data center provisions removed before final passage
fields.key_provisions: SB 197 is the state government agencies budget/appropriations vehicle bill ('AN ACT providing funding and establishing conditions for state government agencies and institutions, making an appropriation therefor, and declaring an emergency'), not a standalone data-center policy bill. House Committee Substitute 1 (2026-03-27) inserted HB 593-style data center electric-service provisions for municipal electric utilities: application/tariff process, $75,000 minimum nonrefundable application fee, 25 MW dedicated-resource threshold, prohibition on subsidizing data center customers via non-data-center rates, and curtailment-allocation rules. That language does not appear in House Committee Substitute 2 (2026-04-15), the version that actually passed both chambers, or in the final enacted bill text. SB 197 was enacted as Acts Ch. 202 (with Governor line-item vetoes of unrelated appropriations items) but contains no data center provisions in its final form.

evidence.title: SB 197 (2026 RS) - Kentucky LRC bill status
evidence.supports: Provides full sponsor list and action history: Senate passage 36-0 (2026-03-06), House passage 82-7 with Committee Substitute (2) (2026-04-15), Senate concurrence 35-1 (2026-04-15), and Governor line-item veto with delivery to Secretary of State as Acts Ch. 202 (2026-04-27). Sponsors are P. Wheeler, S. Madon, S. Funke Frommeyer, R. Mills, R. Webb, not the 'Gex Williams' sponsorship recorded in the prior packet.
evidence.quote: 04/27/26 line items vetoed; delivered to Secretary of State (Acts Ch. 202). Sponsors: P. Wheeler, S. Madon, S. Funke Frommeyer, R. Mills, R. Webb.

evidence.title: SB 197 House Committee Substitute 1 (2026-03-27)
evidence.supports: Shows the data center municipal electric utility provisions that were briefly part of SB 197 mid-session.
evidence.quote: A municipal electric utility shall only provide electric service to a data center customer through a contract that conforms to the requirements of this section...

evidence.title: SB 197 final enacted text
evidence.supports: Confirms no 'data center' language remains in the version that was actually enacted.
evidence.quote: No occurrences of 'data center' found in the final enacted bill text.

decisions.notes: Corrects the packet's sponsor attribution ('Sen. Gex Williams') to the actual LRC-recorded sponsors (P. Wheeler, S. Madon, S. Funke Frommeyer, R. Mills, R. Webb). Also clarifies that while SB 197's data-center policy language died (stripped in the final House Committee Substitute), SB 197 as a bill vehicle was itself enacted into law as Acts Ch. 202, since it is fundamentally a state government appropriations bill unrelated to data centers apart from the language it briefly carried.
